autotools.configuration.makefile.configu: Build configurations (eg, Debug, Release, Full, Minimal, etc)
The name of this build configuration. Appears in the 'Build Configurations' dropdown, and on the status bar.
autotools.configurations.top_builddir.ti: The build directory where 'configure' will be run
autotools.configurations.top_builddir.ma:
Object files and build products will be output in this directory.

Can be an absolute directory, relative (to workspace folder), or empty (meaning 'in-tree' or builddir=srcdir, and not recommended because it prevents other configurations being built.

Also see [GNU autoconf: configurations](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Configuration-Actions.html)
autotools.configurations.makeArgs.markdo:
Arguments to pass to make when building and testing. Used to configure how make runs, but not what it does. (eg, `--no-builtin-rules`, `--load-average`, etc, but not `--directory` or `--touch`).

Also see https://www.gnu.org/software/make/manual/html_node/Options-Summary.html
autotools.configurations.configureArgs.m:
See `configure --help` pallette command for valid options. These arguments can specify optional features to be enabled/disabled/customized (eg `--enable-bigfiles`), or tools (eg. `CXX=g++-13`).

These args are used to prepare top_builddir for building the project.

`--enable-option-checking=fatal` is recommended to combat misspelt options.

Also see [option checking](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.67/html_node/Option-Checking.html)
autotools.welcome.convert.markdownDescri:
This project does not use the autotools build system.
[Add autotools](command:autotools.addAutotools)

This creates a trivial `configure.ac`. A better solution would be to describe the project to a AI chat bot, to generate a set of configure.ac and Makefile.am to your specific needs, as well as iterate using natural language.
autotools.welcome.debug.auto.markdownDes:
Individual tests in [Automake Test Suites](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/Parallel-Test-Harness.html) are debuggable without a launch.json file using settings autodetected by the Autotools integration.

Also see [debug guide](https://Autotools.Mergesium.com/debug).
autotools.welcome.markdownDescription:
No configurations for this autotools project exist yet.
[Create a configuration](command:autotools.newConfiguration)
A 'configuration' means a build directory, a name, and optionally a set of arguments for the configure script.

The project's 'configure' script will be run in the build directory to generate Makefiles, programs can be built using 'Run Task'/build, /check or /test in the build directory.

Ex. configurations: 'Debug', 'Release', etc.
autotools.welcome.debug.markdownDescript: Autotools debug features are available, eg, by clicking the 'Debug' button on a failing unit test in the [Autotools Outline](command:autotools.outline.focus).
autotools.configuration.makefile.configu: Problem matcher names to use when building the current target
autotools.configuration.makefile.logging: The logging level for the makefile tools extension
autotools.configuration.makefile.configu: The path to a cache file storing the output of the last dry-run make command. When unset, a file named 'configurationCache.log' is stored at the path specified by the 'makefile.extensionOutputFolder' setting.
autotools.configuration.autoreconfTool.m: Name of the `autoreconf` tool. Can be used to select a non-default version (eg. `autoreconf2.53`). It must match the version of the autoconf tool.
autotools.configuration.autoBootstrap.ma:
Automatically bootstrap project if the `configure` file does not exist. If disabled, the user will be prompted when bootstrapping is needed.

This allows the ability to manually bootstrap project with non-straightforward requirements.

Also see [bootstrapping](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/faq/autotools-faq.html#What-does-_002e_002fbootstrap-or-_002e_002fautogen_002esh-do_003f)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnCr:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about issues related to cross-compilation. If you must use constructs that prevent cross compilation, set this to `no-cross` to avoid the warning.

Also see [Hosts and Cross-Compilation](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Hosts-and-Cross_002dCompilation.html)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnPo:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about issues related to portability (eg, using `bash` language instead of portable macros like AS_ECHO). Maintainers should set this to `portability` generate the most portable configure scripts.

 References:
  * [Common Shell Constructs](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.68/html_node/Common-Shell-Constructs.html),
  * [Portable Shell](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Portable-Shell.html#Portable-Shell),
  * [Portable Make](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Portable-Make.html#Portable-Make), and
  * [Portable C/C++](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Portable-C-and-C_002b_002b.html#Portable-C-and-C_002b_002b)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnOb:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about obsolete macros (eg, using `AC_CHECK_TYPE` and others).

These warnings indicate the `configure.ac` file is targetting an older autoconf than you are using.

Instead of overriding, consider:

  * using the older autoconf (**autoconf/autoreconf Tool** below), or,

  * updating `configures.ac` to use the newer constructs, as per the autoconf docs

Also see [Obsolete Macros](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Obsolete-Macros.html#Obsolete-Macros)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnOv:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about user redefinitions of Automake rules or variables.

Also see [Automake -Woverride](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/automake-Invocation.html#index-_002dW)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnGn:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about minor deviations from the GNU Coding Standards.

Also see [GNU Coding Standards](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/manual/html_node/Standard-Targets.html)
autotools.configuration.autoreconfWarnUn:
When (re-)generating the configure script, whether to warn about unsupported or incomplete automake features.

Also see [Automake -Wunsupported](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/automake-Invocation.html#index-_002dW)
autotools.configuration.makefile.keepDry: Keep the output of the dry-run in `${top_builddir}/.vscode/${currentTarget}.dryrun.log`
autotools.configuration.makefile.keepCon:
Keep the Intellisense configuration parsed from the makefile as `${top_builddir}/.vscode/${currentTarget}.cache`.

 If this file exists when starting vscode, it will be loaded before dry-running. This can be used to **speed up** Intellisense initialization in very large projects where dry-running is slow.
autotools.configuration.promptClean.desc:
Prompt to clean build directory when the build configuration changes. If disabled, no prompt will be shown, `make clean` will not be run.

Cleaning is advised after: changing `CFLAGS`-like options with a global project impact. Not normally needed after adding or removing dependencies or features
autotools.configuration.tests_environmen: Named set of environment settings, selectable in the testing UI
autotools.configuration.test_environment:
Array of tests environments to run the test suites with.
Each environment has a name and a list of environemnt variable definitions

The name of the test environemnt. Appears in the testing UI to allow selection, and in test grid reports as column names.
Must be a single word. Valid characters: alphanumeric, dash, underscore
List of test suite directories where this environment is used. If missing, environment exists in all test suites.
autotools.configuration.tests_environmen: Set of environment variables set on every test suite run.

Set of environment variables set to every `make check` run. This is the global set, applied to every test in every environment. Variables here can be overriden by setting a different value in a test-environment

This is the only mechanism for passing runtime arguments to automake tests.

Global list of tests expected to fail (XFAIL).
This list applies to all test environments.

Tests marked as `XFAIL` either here or in a test environment can be filtered in the Test Explorer using the `@mergesium.autotools:xfail` filter.
This can be seen as a **TODO** list before release.

Collection of environment variables to set in the tests environment.
Each set is concatenated with the global TESTS_ENVIRONMENT set of variables if defined, and used to set the TESTS_ENVIRONMENTS variable on the `make check` command, eg. `make check TESTS_ENVIRONMENT="\"VAR1=val1\" \"VAR2=val2\""`

see https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/Parallel-Test-Harness.html

List of tests expected to fail (XFAIL) in this test environment.
It is concatenated with the global XFAIL_TESTS.

This is useful as temporary failure waivers during development.

Tests marked as XFAIL do not cause the Test Explorer to mark the global status as '**Failed**'
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.bootstrap: Task bootstraps the autotools project (ie, creates the 'configure' file, see [bootstrap](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/faq/autotools-faq.html#What-does-_002e_002fbootstrap-or-_002e_002fautogen_002esh-do_003f))
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.regen.mar: Task updates Makefile (ie, runs the 'AC_OUTPUT'/config.status, see [Autoconf output](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.69/html_node/Output.html))
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.build.des: Task builds a make target (program, library, etc)
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.test.desc: Task runs one test, named in the 'target' member
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.check.des: Task runs the test suite, ie 'make check'
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.check.tes:
If given, will add a TESTS=... variable to make to limit the run to the specified tests.

Also see [GNU automake parallel test suite](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/Parallel-Test-Harness.html)
autotools.taskDefinitions.task.check.log:
If given, will add a TEST_SUITE_LOG=... variable to make to output the check run to the specified file.

Also see [GNU automake parallel test suite](https://www.gnu.org/software/automake/manual/html_node/Parallel-Test-Harness.html)
autotools.taskDefinitions.target.builddi: Directory where make will be run. Should be a relative dir from the workspace root, and will be prefixed with the configuration directory for out-of-tree builds, then used as the make cwd. Eg, a builddir of 'src' and a configuration of '/tmp/myapp/Debug' and a goal of 'prog' will run 'make -C /tmp/myapp/Debug/src prog'
autotools.taskDefinitions.target.goal.de: Name of the goal as defined in the Makefile (eg, all, check, myprogram.exe, mylib.a, etc)
autotools.taskDefinitions.target.descrip: Definition of the target to be built
Directory where the test or suite will be run
autotools.taskDefinitions.test.goal.desc: Name of the test log file to be refreshed (basename is test name's basename), or 'check'. It will be run with 'make -C $builddir --always-make $goal'
autotools.taskDefinitions.test.descripti: Definition of the test or suite to be run
autotools.taskDefinitions.action.descrip: Autotools action to be performed (bootstrap, update, etc)
autotools.taskDefinitions.label.descript: Description of this task, visible in the command pallete
